title: Missed Opportunity: Critical Minerals and the U.S.-Vietnam Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
gist: Despite a 2023 elevation to Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, U.S.-Vietnam semiconductor and critical-minerals cooperation has stalled amid tariff disputes, a sharp downward revision of Vietnam's rare earth reserves, warming Sino-Vietnamese ties, and reduced U.S. emphasis on great-power competition, leaving China's refining dominance unchallenged.

insights.claim: The 2023 U.S.-Vietnam Comprehensive Strategic Partnership centered on a semiconductor partnership with $2 million U.S. seed funding plus a $1.6 billion Amkor Technology factory in Bac Ninh and two design centers in Ho Chi Minh City, but follow-through on critical minerals commitments has been minimal.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Marquee commitments have not converted to mineral-sector execution, tempering expectations for near-term U.S.-Vietnam supply-chain deals.
insights.quote: follow-through on the 2023 U.S.-Vietnam critical minerals commitments has been minimal

insights.claim: An October 2025 U.S.-Vietnam framework trade agreement cut U.S. tariffs on Vietnamese goods from 46 to 20 percent but included no provisions on critical minerals or transshipment.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Tariff relief without mineral provisions signals minerals remain a dropped thread, not an active workstream.
insights.quote: the deal included no provisions on critical minerals, and Hanoi has stressed it remains only a framework

insights.claim: U.S. tariffs on Vietnamese goods have whipsawed, kept at 20 percent in October 2025, reduced to 10 percent after a February 2026 Supreme Court ruling, then readjusted to 12.5 percent after Section 301 investigations.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Persistent tariff volatility unsettles bilateral trade and consumes the policy bandwidth that mineral cooperation would need.

insights.claim: China holds roughly 70 percent of global rare earth mining capacity and 90 percent of refining capacity, and has weaponized this via 2023 gallium and germanium export restrictions and 2025 curbs on seven rare earths after Trump's 'Liberation Day' tariffs.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: China's refining chokehold and demonstrated willingness to restrict exports is the central risk driving Western diversification and stockpiling.
insights.quote: China holds roughly 70 percent of global rare earth mining capacity and 90 percent of refining capacity
insights.locator: The Strategic Significance of Critical Minerals

insights.claim: Global demand for critical minerals is projected to grow nearly sixfold by 2040 as the clean energy transition accelerates.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A steep demand curve intensifies the strategic value of any non-Chinese supply and refining capacity.
insights.quote: Global demand for critical minerals is projected to grow nearly sixfold by 2040
insights.locator: The Strategic Significance of Critical Minerals

insights.claim: In February 2026 the U.S. hosted a Critical Minerals Ministerial with 54 countries—notably not Vietnam—building on the Pax Silica framework and the 14-member Minerals Security Partnership.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Vietnam's exclusion from the key U.S.-led mineral coalition underscores its marginalization from Western supply-chain architecture.
insights.locator: The Strategic Significance of Critical Minerals

insights.claim: The USGS revised Vietnam's rare earth estimate from roughly 22 million metric tons in 2024 (then world's second largest) down to 3.5 million metric tons in its 2025 report, dropping Vietnam from second to sixth in global reserve rankings behind Brazil, India, Australia, and Russia.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A near-85 percent reserve downgrade sharply reduces Vietnam's leverage as a rare-earth alternative to China.
insights.quote: previously estimated at roughly 22 million metric tons in 2024—then the world’s second largest—to 3.5 million metric tons in its 2025 report

insights.claim: Vietnam's 2023 plan targeted processing over 2 million tons of rare earths annually by 2030, yet actual extraction reached only 600 tons in 2023 and 300 tons in 2024, with corruption prosecutions freezing operations at the Dong Pao mine.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A three-orders-of-magnitude gap between target and output shows Vietnam's rare-earth ambitions are far from investable near term.
insights.quote: actual extraction reached only 600 tons in 2023 and 300 tons in 2024
insights.locator: Vietnam's Strengths and Weaknesses as a Critical Minerals Supplier

insights.claim: Vietnam's real mineral strengths lie outside rare earths: it holds roughly 18 percent of global bauxite reserves and is the world's second-largest tungsten producer, a mineral central to defense manufacturing.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Redirects the Vietnam supply-chain thesis toward bauxite and tungsten rather than the diminished rare-earth story.
insights.quote: it is the world’s second-largest producer of tungsten, a mineral central to defense manufacturing
insights.locator: Vietnam's Strengths and Weaknesses as a Critical Minerals Supplier

insights.claim: Indonesia's 2014 raw-nickel export ban is cited as a cautionary tale: it forced domestic refining but deepened dependence on Chinese technology, did little for local labor, and worsened environmental and social tensions.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Warns that Vietnam's export-restriction-driven refining push could similarly entrench Chinese tech dependence rather than build autonomy.
insights.quote: it has done little to benefit Indonesia’s own labor force while deepening the country’s dependence on Chinese technology to export nickel
insights.locator: Vietnam's Strengths and Weaknesses as a Critical Minerals Supplier

insights.claim: Warming Sino-Vietnamese ties—Xi's 2023 and 2025 Hanoi visits, To Lam's 2024 Beijing trip as his first overseas visit as general secretary, and dozens of new economic agreements—reduce the strategic logic for U.S.-Vietnam mineral cooperation.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Hanoi's hedge toward Beijing narrows the window for U.S. supply-chain gains in Vietnam.

insights.claim: The second Trump administration's 2025 National Security Strategy and 2026 National Defense Strategy both downplay great-power competition and omit Vietnam entirely, diminishing Southeast Asia's strategic salience for the U.S.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Reduced U.S. strategic prioritization means Vietnam cooperation will rest on commercial rather than geopolitical logic.
insights.quote: both downplay great power competition and omit Vietnam entirely

insights.claim: The U.S. purchases nearly 30 percent of Vietnam's exports, making Washington indispensable to Hanoi's goal of upper-middle-income status by 2030 and advanced-economy status by 2045.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: U.S. market access remains Vietnam's key dependency and the primary lever Washington retains despite the minerals stall.
insights.quote: The United States purchases nearly 30 percent of Vietnam’s exports
